name: kimi-ahk-design-csv
goal:
You are the campaign ARCHITECT for module 3 of your plan (PLAN.md): csv.ahk - parse a CSV/DSV STRING into a 1-based array of 1-based row arrays, and serialize fields and rows back with correct quoting. Modules 1 and 2 are DONE and approved by the PM: str.ahk (your contract ahk_str.md, Hoss + Qwen, first try) and regex.ahk (your contract ahk_regex.md, Nemotron on attempt 3, Hoss's tests first try). Use those two contracts as the structural model.

WHAT THE SANDBOX TAUGHT US - read this twice. Both your earlier designs were right about the code and wrong on AutoHotkey facts you REASONED instead of OBSERVED: title case breaks words only at spaces (not hyphens or apostrophes); multiline regex (m)) treats only CRLF as a line break by default, not a bare `n. Both are now in the playbooks, which you should read. For csv.ahk the risky facts are: how StrSplit, InStr, SubStr and Loop, Parse behave on empty fields, a trailing delimiter, a trailing line break, `r`n vs `n, and a quote inside an unquoted field; and what == says when comparing "" with a field. Every expected value in your tests that you have not seen real AutoHotkey produce goes on your final list - the PA runs your reference against your tests in Windows Sandbox and fixes what AutoHotkey disagrees with before any crew member sees the contract.

THE PA'S DECISIONS: API as in your plan - CsvParse(text, delim := ",", encap := """"), CsvEscape(cell, delim := ",", encap := """"), CsvRow(fields, delim := ",", encap := """") - unless you find a reason to change it, which you state. Lenient parsing, like the stock library (PA answer to your question 4): a stray quote inside an unquoted field is literal text; state exactly what an unterminated quoted field at the end of the text does. CRLF and LF both end a row; a line break INSIDE a quoted field is data and is kept as it was written. Say exactly what a trailing line break, a blank line in the middle and a completely empty text return. csv.ahk is SELF-CONTAINED (depends on nothing) - the parser is a character loop, it does not need regex.ahk. Team: author Hoss, tester Qwen (your plan).

FIXED RULES OF THE JUDGE: crew/contracts/ahk_scan.md (no '%', no loose code, no banned words, no hotkeys or labels) and ahk_api.md. Tests start with exactly `#Include tap.ahk` then `#Include csv.ahk`, use only Is(got, want, name) and Ok(cond, name), end with Done(). Arrays compare by reference: check Length() and each element. A literal quote inside an AutoHotkey string is written "" and a line break is `n (backtick) - never backslash.

STAGE EXACTLY THESE FILES with stage_file:
1. csv.md - the contract (structure of ahk_regex.md: purpose, Public API, numbered rules with examples, edge cases stated outright, 'A careless implementation cannot pass').
2. csv.ahk - your reference implementation.
3. test_csv.ahk - hidden tests: at least 35 Is/Ok checks, each naming its rule; include round-trip checks (parse what CsvRow produced).
4. campaign.json - EXACTLY the shape of crew/campaigns/ahk_regex.json (read it: top-level name, senior, senior_fallback, max_attempts, max_escalations, max_requests, workspace_subdir, goal, teams {TeamName: {author, tester}}, tasks [ {id, team, module, contract, hidden_tests, api, depends, min_tests, instructions, test_instructions} ]). Last time your campaign.json used a different shape and the PA had to rebuild it. Use name "ahk-csv", team "Tables" {author Hoss, tester Qwen}, task id "csv", module "csv.ahk", contract "C:/Users/user/ATLAS-api-harness/crew/contracts/ahk_csv.md", hidden_tests ["C:/Users/user/ATLAS-api-harness/crew/hidden_tests/test_csv.ahk"], depends [], min_tests 16, workspace_subdir "ahk_lib".

Final answer: the API in one paragraph, then EVERY check in test_csv.ahk whose expected value you have not seen real AutoHotkey produce, as a list.
